chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Buddy Harper, Paul Howard's group and Ted Brinson
summary: Willard reads a 1942 Paul Howard personnel; Spikes notes Ted Brinson, a mailman with his own studio.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Buddy Harper. We were talking about Buddy Harper off the tape. I think Buddy Harper played guitar...and arranger and...
Yeah, and he's very good, too.

Mmmm hmmm. That's right. I heard Buddy...I heard the big band up at the Union a couple of years ago, that Buddy had put together. I guess that's the same band he has taken around to the prisons now. Very good.

It says, uh...piano...uh... Paul Howard fronted a group, and he was on tenor saxophone. It says, "Down Beat of 1st of November 1942 listed the rest of the personnel as Earl Willis (piano), Buddy Harper (guitar), Ted Brinson (string bass) and Willis McDaniels (drums)."

Ted Brinson has got a recording studio. He's a mailman in here--he's been for twenty, twenty-five years, but he's got a recording studio that he does, you know, in his spare time at Fifth Avenue and Washington upstairs there. He's been up there twenty, twenty-some years. Ted Brinson. But he's a mailman around in this district.
